label: intended
prompt:
MySQL table options may be separated by spaces instead of commas (CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB), and CHARSET / CHAR SET are synonyms of CHARACTER SET, also on columns. sqlglot does not accept these forms; they should parse, CHARSET should be written as CHARACTER SET, and in ALTER TABLE the options should be written comma-separated after the actions.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("CREATE TABLE t (a VARCHAR(5) CHARSET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin) CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ParseError: Expecting ). Line 1, Col: 36.
# expected:  CREATE TABLE t (a VARCHAR(5) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin) CHARACTER SET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB

parse_one("ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a VARCHAR(5) CHARSET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a VARCHAR(5) CHARSET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB
# expected:  ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a VARCHAR(5) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, CHARACTER SET=utf8mb4, ENGINE=InnoDB
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.

+    OPTIONAL_COMMA_BETWEEN_ALTER_TABLE_OPTIONS: t.ClassVar = False

     ALTER_TABLE_PARTITIONS: t.ClassVar = False
 
@@ -3038,6 +3041,8 @@ class Parser:
             for p in ensure_list(prop):
                 properties.append(p)
 
+            self._match(TokenType.COMMA, expression=properties[-1])

             return self.expression(exp.Properties(expressions=properties))
 
@@ -9417,7 +9422,11 @@ class Parser:
                 actions.extend(parsed)
 
             not_valid = self._match_text_seq("NOT", "VALID")

prompt:
MySQL table options may be separated by spaces instead of commas (CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB), and CHARSET / CHAR SET are synonyms of CHARACTER SET, also on columns. sqlglot does not accept these forms; they should parse, CHARSET should be written as CHARACTER SET, and in ALTER TABLE the options should be written comma-separated after the actions.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("CREATE TABLE t (a VARCHAR(5) CHARSET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin) CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ParseError: Expecting ). Line 1, Col: 36.
# expected:  CREATE TABLE t (a VARCHAR(5) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin) CHARACTER SET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB

parse_one("ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a VARCHAR(5) CHARSET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a VARCHAR(5) CHARSET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB
# expected:  ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a VARCHAR(5) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, CHARACTER SET=utf8mb4, ENGINE=InnoDB
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.
